Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat

Class SendMessageService

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.SendMessageService
All Implemented Interfaces:
SendMessageUseCase
@Service public class SendMessageService extends Object implements SendMessageUseCase
Default SendMessageUseCase implementation (US-11-004).

Architecture: a synchronous prefix followed by a reactive tail.

  • The synchronous prefix runs inside the @Transactional boundary of send(SendMessageCommand): load + verify conversation, check cap, persist USER message, derive title on first turn. Failures propagate as exceptions out of send(com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.SendMessageUseCase.SendMessageCommand) — Spring maps them to the matching application/problem+json body and the SSE stream is never opened.
  • The reactive tail (returned Flux) emits TurnEvent.Started, then maps the LLM's chunk stream to TurnEvent.Deltas, and on completion persists the ASSISTANT message inside a SECOND transaction (via TransactionTemplate because the reactive callback runs outside the @Transactional method invocation).

The LlmChatClient is injected as an Optional rather than required. In test profiles where Spring AI's OpenAI autoconfig is excluded (Spring AI 1.1.0 / Spring 7 binary incompat — see OpenAiChatClientAdapter), no LlmChatClient bean exists and send(SendMessageCommand) fails fast on first invocation with IllegalStateException (mapped to 500 INTERNAL_ERROR by the generic handler). This pattern lets the bean always exist — every @SpringBootTest in the suite still boots green — while still failing fast and coherently when an actual chat turn is attempted without a configured provider. The 500 (rather than 502) is correct: a missing LLM provider in production is an operator misconfiguration, not an upstream availability issue.

  • Method Details

    • send

      @Transactional public reactor.core.publisher.Flux<TurnEvent> send(SendMessageUseCase.SendMessageCommand command)
      Description copied from interface: SendMessageUseCase
      Runs the chat turn.

      Behavior:

      1. Synchronous prefix: load + verify conversation, check messageCount < 64, persist USER message (transactional), derive title on first message. Throws synchronously on failure; the Flux is never returned in that case.
      2. Reactive tail: emit TurnEvent.Started, build memory window + ChatRequest, stream from the LLM emitting one TurnEvent.Delta per chunk, then on completion persist the ASSISTANT message and emit TurnEvent.Completed.
